Class SlowQueryReport.PoolStatistics

java.lang.Object
org.apache.tomcat.jdbc.pool.interceptor.SlowQueryReport.PoolStatistics
Enclosing class:
SlowQueryReport
protected static class SlowQueryReport.PoolStatistics extends Object
The query statistics of one pool: the map its connections book into and the name the map is published under.

The store refers to the pool only weakly. The name identifies the pool and must be unique among live pools - Tomcat names every pool it manages, and the default name of a programmatic pool is unique as well - so the store can outlive a pool abandoned without closing without pinning that pool, together with everything it reaches: its queues, its pooled connections and their open physical sessions. The weak reference is what tells a live holder of the name from an abandoned pool's leftover store.

    • setJmxState

      protected void setJmxState(SlowQueryReportJmx.PoolJmx jmxState)
      Records what the reporting subclass has published for this pool, so that the release of this store gives it up. Callers publish one state per store under this store's monitor (see SlowQueryReportJmx).
      Parameters:
      jmxState - the state to hang from this store

    • release

      protected void release()
      Releases the store with the close of its pool: later reads of its statistics answer as if nothing were published, and the JMX state published for this pool is given up with it.

      Whether a state exists is decided under this store's monitor, which is the one a borrow publishes a new state under, so no state can be created behind the release and left for nothing to give up. The state's own release then runs outside the monitor: it gives the MBean back to the MBeanServer, and a close has no business holding the store while it does.
